text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 1.3% today, continuing a sharp two-week slide that has erased roughly 9% of the stock's value since mid-September. The immediate trigger appears to be oil price weakness: crude dropped today after Iran signaled willingness to return to nuclear negotiations and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, easing geopolitical tensions that had been supporting prices. With US oil trading at $96.41 per barrel—down sharply from where it was two weeks ago—refiners' ability to turn crude into profitable fuel margins has compressed.

The broader backdrop adds pressure. Refineries are running at 94% capacity while gasoline and diesel inventories sit at elevated levels, meaning there's less urgency to run hard and less room for margin expansion even if crude prices stabilize. On top of that, ongoing debate over a potential diesel export ban creates regulatory uncertainty that could ultimately reduce refining activity—the opposite of what would help the stock recover.
